24 import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner; 25 26 /** 27 * Repository class for Owner domain objects All method names are compliant with Spring Data naming 28 * conventions so this interface can easily be extended for Spring Data See here: http://static.springsource.org/spring-data/jpa/docs/current/reference/html/jpa.repositories.html#jpa.query-methods.query-creation 29 * 30 * @author Ken Krebs 31 * @author Juergen Hoeller 32 * @author Sam Brannen 33 * @author Michael Isvy 34 * @author Vitaliy Fedoriv 35 */ 36 public interface OwnerRepository { 37 38 /** 39 * Retrieve Owners from the data store by last name, returning all owners whose last name starts 40 * with the given name. 41 * 42 * @param lastName Value to search for 43 * @return a Collection of matching Owners (or an empty Collection if none 44 * found) 45 */ 46 Collection findByLastName(String lastName) throws DataAccessException; 47 48 Page findByLastName(String lastName, Pageable pageable) throws DataAccessException; 49 50 /** 51 * Retrieve an Owner from the data store by id. 52 * 53 * @param id the id to search for 54 * @return the Owner if found 55 * @throws org.springframework.dao.DataRetrievalFailureException if not found 56 */ 57 Owner findById(int id) throws DataAccessException; VERDICT: LGTM

The change slots cleanly into the existing structure and matches this codebase's established idioms.

- **`countNamesakes` placement and style** mirror the existing private helpers in the same class. It sits right next to `generateCustomerCode`, uses the same `ownerRepository.findAll().stream()` filtering approach already used by `isTelephoneInUse`, `isHouseholdInUse`, and `generateCustomerCode` (the repository exposes no derived count query, so this is the conventional unit here), and carries a javadoc consistent with its neighbors.
- **`saveOwner` refactor** is coherent: namesakeCount is a derived-on-create field computed alongside the existing derived `customerCode`, correctly guarded by `owner.isNew()`, and the `if (... == null)` guard mirrors the customer-code guard so a caller-supplied value is respected. No catch-all growth — the new logic is a sibling of what was already there.
- **Model getter/setter and field** follow the standard Owner accessor pattern.
- **Schema changes** are applied uniformly across all four dialects, and the OpenAPI `namesakeCount` entry matches the surrounding read-only property style.

Nothing is duplicated or misplaced; a maintainer would find this natural.
